data.exact_reserve_text: During the year, the Syndicate released GBP 9.6m of technical reserves in respect of prior years (2020: GBP 9.5m) arising from the nuclear property and nuclear liability classes (2020: from the nuclear property and nuclear liability classes).

named_events.loss_description: One significant core melt nuclear event paid by the insurance market.
Fukushima accident in March 2011 prompted extensive review of potential catastrophe exposure; exposure considered to be limited following analysis.

named_events.event_name: Hurricane Andrew (spares warehouse loss on a nuclear site)
named_events.loss_description: Largest insured windstorm loss to date was from a spares warehouse on a nuclear site from Hurricane Andrew in 1992; losses in the region of $200m, with no damage to the nuclear unit.
Limited underwriting exposure; all significant insured sites have operated throughout the pandemic and there is no known specific pandemic cover offered.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 1176 opened 2021 with gross claims outstanding of GBP 38.419m. During 2021 the Syndicate reported a release of technical reserves of GBP 9.6m in respect of prior years, driven by favourable prior-year claims development primarily in its nuclear property and nuclear liability business. The release materially improved results for prior years; no detailed split of the release by line of business was provided.
raw_causal_phrases: During the year, the Syndicate released GBP 9.6m of technical reserves in respect of prior years (2020: GBP 9.5m) arising from the nuclear property and nuclear liability classes (2020: from the nuclear property and nuclear liability classes).
The reduction in net incurred claims in 2021 is mainly driven by favourable prior year development
We have received very few claims and those we did receive were settled at less than reserved.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development amount (-GBP 9.6m) was taken from Note 4 narrative stating a release of GBP 9.6m. The note does not explicitly state 'gross' but context and placement in technical reserves suggests this refers to gross technical reserves; confidence reduced accordingly. A gross claims development triangle is present in Note 18 but the OCR/formatting in source made reliable automated extraction of every cell difficult; therefore the triangle was not used to recalculate PYD. No LOB-level split of the GBP 9.6m release was provided.
